title: Operational Contracts Kickoff and Ramp Playbook Q2 2026
content:
Purpose:
This playbook organizes the first 8-week cross-functional ramp to establish operational contracts (SLOs/SLO indicators + ownership + runbooks) for two priority surfaces: hosted API (text generation) and dedicated GPU clusters. It’s meant to be a practical, minimal-lift plan to get measurable SLOs, alerting, and a basic incident response flow in place so product teams and customers have predictable behavior and clear escalation paths.

Background/context (short):
- Several product teams requested explicit SLOs for latency and availability for hosted inference endpoints and for Dedicated capacity SLAs.
- Current observability covers many signals but lacks consistent SLI definitions, ownership, and documented fallback behavior (e.g., model variant routing).
- Goal: define and operationalize SLOs that map to business/customer expectations and can be monitored/acted on by SRE + product + infra + runtime.

Scope (what we will do in this ramp):
- Define two canonical SLOs per product surface: Availability SLO and Latency SLO (p95/p99).
- Standardize SLI definitions (request success, server error taxonomy, client retry behavior, cold-start contribution).
- Build dashboard + alerting (Grafana + PagerDuty) for SLO burn and error budget.
- Create 1 runbook per surface and a shared on-call rotation play for escalations.
- Execute a single canary test + simulated traffic run to validate thresholds.
- Draft operator-facing operational contract template for future teams.

Out of scope for this ramp:
- Full legal SLA/contract signatures (we will provide inputs for sales/finance).
- Deep model quality/regression monitoring (will be coordinated with Optimize/Applied ML separately).

Success criteria (measurable):
- Two SLO documents (hosted API, dedicated clusters) with owner and SLI defs finalized.
- Dashboards showing 7d/30d burn rate + automated alerting when burn > 10% in 24h.
- One successful canary run where traffic is shifted and metrics tracked end-to-end.
- Runbooks verified in tabletop exercise with SRE and at least one product owner.

Stakeholders and responsibilities (high level):
- Eng-SRE (Elena Park): overall program lead, alerting, runbooks, on-call integration.
- Serving Runtime (Marcus Li): instrumentation points, latency breakdowns, failure modes.
- Platform/Infra (Priya Desai): cluster health, Dedicated capacity telemetry, autoscale knobs.
- Product: Hosted API PM (Omar Fernandez) and Dedicated PM (Noah Reed): acceptance criteria, customer impact definitions, business thresholds.
- Observability (Platform monitoring team): dashboards + retention questions.
- Solutions Engineering / CS: customer-facing operational contract template and FAQ.

Milestone calendar (8 weeks)
- Week 0 (Kickoff): align on goals, invite list, initial SLI candidates, map existing signals. (Owner: Elena)
- Week 1: finalize SLI definitions and data pipelines required (metrics and logs). (Owners: Marcus + Priya)
  - Deliverable: SLI spec doc with metric names, tags, and known blind spots.
- Week 2: draft SLO targets (p95 latency, availability target) and sign-off workshop with PMs. (Owners: Product + Elena)
  - Deliverable: SLO draft for hosted API and dedicated clusters.
- Week 3: instrument missing metrics and validate telemetry; small telemetry follow-up sprint. (Owners: Runtime + Infra)
  - Deliverable: queries that compute SLIs in Grafana/Prom.
- Week 4: dashboards and alert rules implemented; link to PagerDuty and escalation policy drafted. (Owner: Observability)
  - Deliverable: Dashboards + alert rule PRs.
- Week 5: runbook drafting and tabletop exercise. (Owner: SRE)
  - Deliverable: Two runbooks and exercise notes.
- Week 6: canary + simulated traffic test on hosted API; measure SLO performance and iterate. (Owners: Runtime + SRE)
  - Deliverable: Canary report and action items.
- Week 7: dedicate time for Dedicated cluster validation and soak tests; finalize operational contract template. (Owners: Infra + Solutions Eng)
  - Deliverable: Dedicated cluster playbook and template.
- Week 8: handoff, retro, and post-mortem of the ramp. (Owner: Elena)
  - Deliverable: Retro doc, list of follow-ups and backlog tickets.

Sprint/Task breakdown (examples):
- SLI spec task: list metric name, query, expected tags, edge cases, owner, acceptance criteria. (ticket: JIRA-SRE-1142)
- Latency taxonomy: break down p50/p95/p99 by model size, sequence length, cold-start, serve queue. Owner: Marcus Li.
- Error classification: define transient vs persistent, map HTTP 5xx codes to 'user visible failure' vs internal degrade. Owner: Priya Desai.
- Dashboard templating: single dashboard panel template to reuse across services. Owner: Observability.
- PagerDuty integration: ensure runbook links in PD incidents and auto-assign rules. Owner: Elena.

Roles and contact points (day-to-day):
- SLO Owner (per-surface): Product PM — responsible for business thresholds and sign-off.
- Metrics Steward: Runtime engineer — ensures telemetry correctness.
- On-call escalator: SRE shift lead — owns incident response per runbook.
- Contract custodian: Solutions Eng — owns customer-facing wording.

Dependencies and constraints:
- Need additional metrics instrumentation in runtime (may require 2-day engineering spike).
- Grafana/Prom retention limits may obscure long tail percentiles; consider short-term retention bump for this project.
- PagerDuty rule limit requires consolidation of alerts to avoid noise.

Risk register (top 5):
- Instrumentation gaps lead to incorrect SLOs -> mitigation: conservative SLO targets, sign-off only after telemetry validation.
- Alert fatigue due to poorly-scoped rules -> mitigation: use burn-rate + cardinality thresholds before PD page.
- Capacity constraints during canary causing customer-visible outages -> mitigation: schedule tests in low-traffic windows, throttle traffic.
- Conflicting product goals (latency vs model quality) -> mitigation: require product sign-off and include Optimize/Applied ML in tradeoff doc.
- Ownership ambiguity -> mitigation: assign SLO Owner and Metrics Steward explicitly and add to runbook header.

Communication plan and rituals:
- Weekly 30m sync (Mon 10:00 PST) for rapid unblock + decisions (owner: Elena).
- Bi-weekly stakeholder demo of dashboards + canary results.
- Slack channel: #sre-op-contracts (use for async questions, pin runbook draft).
- Confluence page: canonical SLO docs + linked dashboards (linked_artifacts above).

Tabletop exercise script (1 hour):
- Scenario: sudden p95 latency spike + increased 5xx errors during a model rollout.
- Participants: Product PM, Runtime lead, Infra, Observability, SRE on-call.
- Goals: confirm who paged, confirm mitigation steps (fallback routing, scale-up), confirm communication to customers.

Open questions (to resolve in first 2 weeks):
- Do we want separate availability SLOs for control-plane vs data-plane? (impact on metrics and alerting)
- Should Dedicated capacity have a strict availability SLA or a best-effort SLO with credits handled by sales/legal?
- What burn-rate window is meaningful for user-facing problems (1h, 6h, 24h)?

Immediate action items (first 7 days):
- [Elena] Create kickoff calendar invite and invite list (done).
- [Marcus] Post SLI candidate list to Confluence and tag missing metrics (due: 2026-03-04).
- [Priya] Check Prom retention and estimate cost to bump 30d percentile retention (due: 2026-03-06).
- [Omar] Prepare customer-impact examples for Product sign-off workshop (due: 2026-03-05).

Notes to self / working assumptions:
- Keep SLO targets conservative initially to avoid false positives during telemetry warm-up.
- Use model-agnostic SLO categories (latency availability) first, then add model-specific follow-ups.
- Think of this as a template: once validated, roll out as an org-wide operational contract kit.

Appendix: minimal SLO templates (short)
- Hosted API availability: "Percent requests returning success within backend timeout (30s)". Target: 99.95% monthly. SLI query: sum(success_requests)/sum(total_requests) where success = 2xx within 30s.
- Hosted API latency: "p95 request latency for generation endpoint (excluding warm starts)". Target: p95 < 350ms. SLI query: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) with warm-start label.
- Dedicated cluster availability: "Percent of scheduled capacity available to customer jobs". Target: 99.9% monthly. SLI query: scheduled_capacity_available/contracted_capacity.

If you want to run this as a shorter pilot (4 weeks) we can compress weeks 1–4 and defer Dedicated cluster validation to a follow-up. Otherwise plan as above.

-- Elena
